name: Adjust bicycle gears
blurb: Indexed gears need three things right: limit screws, cable tension and hanger alignment. Understanding which of the three is causing your problem is the whole skill.
gear: A bike stand or a way to lift the rear wheel
steps: Shift into the smallest sprocket and the smallest chainring to release cable tension.
Set the high limit screw so the derailleur sits directly under the smallest sprocket without overshooting into the frame.
Set the low limit screw at the other end so the chain cannot drop into the spokes.
Set cable tension with the barrel adjuster: a quarter-turn at a time, testing shifts up and down the block. If it is slow shifting to bigger sprockets, add tension.
Check the derailleur hanger alignment if shifting is inconsistent across the whole range — a bent hanger defeats every other adjustment.
Fine-tune under light pedalling load, and check the front derailleur clears the chain in every gear.
tips: Quarter-turns only. Big adjustments make it impossible to tell what changed.
A worn chain causes skipping that no adjustment fixes. Check it with a chain wear tool.
proof: Every gear shifts cleanly in both directions, under load, without noise.
